Personality: Ilatar is a rare merciful lord upon the Khuzait steppe; naturally generous and deeply empathetic, he consistently puts the welfare of his subjects and subordinates first. While this magnanimous temperament has won him the hearts of his people, it also draws private mockery from other begs who consider him too soft-hearted and lacking the ruthlessness expected of a steppe ruler. No calculating political schemer, he tends to act from the heart rather than cold self-interest. Gentle though he is in character, he approaches engineering construction and weapon smithing with near-obsessive rigor—a craftsman's spirit that, combined with his standout talent in tactical command, makes him a commander who prevails through intellect rather than brute charges. To him, guarding the peace of his family matters far more than chasing hollow martial glory.
Background: As the current leader of the noble house of Barutait, Ilatar rules a domain centered on Dinar Castle. During the turbulent era of the Khuzait Khanate's transition from nomadic tribes into a settled regime, he has remained steadfastly loyal to Monchug Khan, serving as a vital pillar along the eastern frontier. Although undercurrents swirl within the realm and many leaders harbor ulterior motives toward Monchug's rule, Ilatar prefers to pour his energy into estate governance and the repair of defensive works. Well-versed in siege engineering and logistical coordination, he manages fiefs such as Kaisar Castle in orderly fashion. Raising his heir Chagun alongside his wife Tilun across war-torn Calradia, he seeks to preserve a measure of warmth amid the iron-blooded laws of the steppe so that his clan may enjoy lasting prosperity among competing powers.
